mainTopic: Closing רבי יוסי's view on impurity and the full זבה, then the new perek מי שאמר: when a נזיר shaves, how two terms are counted, and טומאה at the end of a term
overview: The גמרא finishes a talk between רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן. רבי אושעיא says רבי יוסי agrees that the impurity counts only from now on. The גמרא asks how that fits רבי יוסי's ruling that the impurity is retroactive. It answers that the retroactive impurity is only מדרבנן. Next it asks how רבי יוסי, who holds that part of a day counts as a whole day, can ever have a full זבה. It gives two answers: a nonstop flow for three days, or seeing right before sunset each day. Then the perek הריני נזיר closes, and a new perek opens. A plain נזיר shaves on day 31, and day 30 also works. One who said 'thirty days' outright does not fulfill his נזירות by shaving on day 30. The משנה also explains how someone with two terms of נזירות counts his shaving days, and רבי פפייס testifies that day 30 counts toward the second term. Finally the משנה rules on a נזיר who becomes טמא near the end of his term, where רבי אליעזר argues for leniency. The גמרא begins discussing that case.

steps.title: רבי יוסי agrees: impurity counts only from now on
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא tells רבי יוחנן that רבי יוסי holds like him: the impurity takes effect only from this point forward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to him: רבי יוסי holds like you, since he says the person becomes impure from now and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא brings support for רבי יוחנן's view from the opinion of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that for רבי יוסי, impurity that comes after the start of the seventh day works only 'from now on' (מכאן ולהבא). It does not wipe out the clean days already counted. This puts רבי יוסי on רבי יוחנן's side.

keyTerms.meaning: holds like you, agrees with you
from now and onward
is impure / imparts impurity

phrases.english: And he said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אושעיא speaking to רבי יוחנן, continuing their talk from earlier on the daf.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei holds in accordance with you,
as he says he becomes impure from now and onward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רבי אושעיא and רבי יוחנן exchange from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי יוסי, the impurity takes effect only from now on and does not cancel earlier clean days.

steps.title: But רבי יוסי said retroactive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רבי יוסי is known to rule that the impurity is retroactive.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it רבי יוסי who said the impurity is retroactive?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אושעיא's claim. רבי יוסי's known ruling sounds like the opposite of 'from now on'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere רבי יוסי rules 'למפרע', meaning the impurity reaches backward in time. That seems to contradict the claim that he holds 'from now on'. So how can רבי אושעיא cite him as support?

keyTerms.meaning: retroactively, backward in time
but isn't it so that (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But wasn't it Rabbi Yosei
who said it is retroactive!

steps.triggerLanguage: והא רבי יוסי למפרע הוא דאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim made in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's statement that רבי יוסי holds 'from now on'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי's known ruling of 'retroactive' impurity seems to contradict 'from now on'.

steps.title: Retroactive only by rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: The 'retroactive' impurity of רבי יוסי is only מדרבנן. By Torah law it is 'from now on'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'retroactive' mean? Only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: רבי יוסי's 'retroactive' ruling is a rabbinic rule, not Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both statements can be true. מדאורייתא, the impurity counts only from now on, which supports רבי יוחנן. The Rabbis added a stricter retroactive impurity on top of that.

keyTerms.meaning: what (does it mean)?
by rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי: from now on by Torah law; retroactive only מדרבנן.

phrases.english: What is 'retroactive'?
By rabbinic law.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the levels: Torah law versus rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's 'retroactive' meant real Torah-level impurity backward in time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The retroactive impurity is only מדרבנן; by Torah law it is from now on.

steps.title: If part of a day is a whole day, how is there ever a full זבה?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יוסי holds מקצת היום ככולו, the rest of the day after she sees should count as her clean day. Then how could she ever become a full זבה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רבי יוסי: he holds that part of a day is like a whole day. So how can you ever find a full זבה who brings a קרבן? Once she sees in the middle of the day, the other half of the day counts for her as a clean day of watching!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty with רבי יוסי's rule that part of a day counts as a full day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full זבה brings a קרבן only after seeing on three days in a row. If she sees at midday, the rest of that day would already count as a clean 'watching' day. That breaks the chain, so it seems she could never reach three days in a row.

keyTerms.meaning: now, since it is established that
part of the day counts as the whole day
a full זבה (who saw three days in a row)
a clean day of watching

phrases.english: And as for Rabbi Yosei,
now, he holds that part of the day is like all of it;
a full zavah who brings an offering,
how can you find her?
Since she sees in the middle of the day,
the other half of the day
counts for her as watching!
phrases.notes: 'Watching' means a clean day she keeps after seeing blood. Here, the rest of the day would already count as that clean day.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבי יוסי מכדי סבר מקצת היום ככולו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question on רבי יוסי's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's rule of מקצת היום ככולו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rest of any day she sees counts as a clean day, she can never see on three days in a row, so a זבה גמורה could never exist.

steps.title: First answer: she flows for three days straight
steps.stepSummary: She has a nonstop discharge for three days, so there is never a clean part of a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say that she flows continuously for three days in a row.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer: a continuous flow leaves no clean part of any day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of מקצת היום ככולו needs some clean part of a day to count as a watching day. If the blood never stops for three days, no part of those days is clean. So she does become a full זבה.

keyTerms.meaning: if you wish, say (one possible answer)
flows continuously
together, in a row

phrases.english: If you wish, say that she flows continuously
for three days together, one after the other.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a case where the problem does not arise
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed a זבה גמורה was impossible for רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a nonstop flow for three days, there is no clean part of a day.

steps.title: Second answer: she sees right before sunset
steps.stepSummary: She sees on three days, each time close to sunset, so no clean part of a day is left to count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say that she saw on three days, close to sunset, so there was no time left that would count for her in her counting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the same difficulty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she sees just before the sun sets, there is no time left in that day to count as a clean day. That way she sees on three days in a row with no watching day in between, even without a nonstop flow.

keyTerms.meaning: close to sunset
time, an interval
the counting (of days)

steps.whatToRemember: A full זבה is possible for רבי יוסי in two ways: a nonstop flow, or seeing right before sunset each day.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
that she saw on three days
close to sunset,
so that there was no time
that would count for her counting.
phrases.notes: He means the count of clean days. No clean bit of the day was left to count.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואיבעית אימא דחזיא תלתא יומי סמוך לשקיעת החמה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 4, alongside step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different case that avoids the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a nonstop flow could produce a full זבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Seeing near sunset on three days also leaves no clean time, so she becomes a full זבה.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the perek הריני נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the perek הריני נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, הריני נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The perek ends here with the traditional closing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן marks the end of the perek הריני נזיר. It expresses the hope of returning to learn it again. The next line starts a new perek.

keyTerms.meaning: we will return to you (closing formula for a perek)

phrases.english: We will return to you,
'I am hereby a nazirite'
phrases.notes: This is the name of the perek that just ended.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek after the last discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The perek הריני נזיר is complete.

steps.title: When a נזיר shaves: plain vow versus 'thirty days'
steps.stepSummary: A plain נזיר shaves on day 31, and shaving on day 30 still counts. One who said 'thirty days' does not fulfill his נזירות if he shaves on day 30.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who said 'I am hereby a נזיר' shaves on day thirty-one, and if he shaved on day thirty, he has fulfilled his נזירות. If he said 'I am hereby a נזיר for thirty days' and shaved on day thirty, he has not fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new perek opens with a משנה about which day a נזיר may shave at the end of his נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain נזירות lasts thirty days, so the proper shaving day is the 31st, but day 30 is still valid after the fact. When he says 'thirty days' outright, his words show he means thirty full days. So shaving on day 30 is too early.

keyTerms.meaning: shaves (his hair at the end of נזירות)
has fulfilled his obligation
has not fulfilled his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Both people are נזירים for thirty days. The difference is only whether day 30 is valid for shaving, and that depends on whether he said 'thirty days' outright.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic count for an ordinary נזירות. The rest of the perek builds on it.

phrases.english: One who said: 'I am hereby a nazirite'
shaves on the thirty-first day,
and if he shaved on the thirtieth day, he has fulfilled his obligation.
'I am hereby a nazirite for thirty days':
if he shaved on the thirtieth day,
he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: מי שאמר הריני נזיר מגלח יום שלשים ואחד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the new perek after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plain נזיר shaves on day 31, and day 30 is valid after the fact. One who said 'thirty days' outright is not fulfilled by shaving on day 30.

steps.title: Shaving days for someone who took on two terms
steps.stepSummary: Someone with two נזירות normally shaves on day 31 and day 61. If he shaved for the first on day 30, he shaves for the second on day 60, and even day 59 works.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person vowed two נזירות, he shaves for the first on day 31 and for the second on day 61. If he shaved for the first on day 30, he shaves for the second on day 60. If he shaved for the second on day 59, he has still fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the rule from step 8 and applies it to a person who took on two נזירות in a row.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The best way is to finish 30 full days for each term, so he shaves on day 31 and day 61. If he shaved early on day 30, that day still counts toward the first term. It can also count as the first day of the second term, so the second term can end one day earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Two terms of נזירות, one right after the other
He shaves his hair, which marks the end of his נזירות
Less one, meaning one day short
He has fulfilled his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Day 59 works only if he shaved for the first term on day 30. That day 30 does double duty, counting for both terms.

phrases.english: One who vowed two terms of nezirus

phrases.aramaic: מְגַלֵּחַ אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: shaves for the first one on day thirty-one,
and for the second one on day sixty-one.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם גִּילַּח אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים —
phrases.english: And if he shaved for the first one on day thirty
he shaves for the second one on day sixty,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם גִּילַּח יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים חָסֵר אֶחָד —
phrases.english: and if he shaved on day sixty less one
he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the day-30 rule from step 8 to a person with two terms in a row.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ideally he shaves on days 31 and 61. If he shaved for the first term on day 30, he may shave for the second on day 60, and day 59 also works.

steps.title: רבי פפייס testifies to the same rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי פפייס testified to this same law and gave the reason: day 30 counts toward the second term's tally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פפייס gave this testimony about someone who vowed two נזירות. If he shaved for the first on day 30, he shaves for the second on day 60. If he shaved on day 59, he has fulfilled it, because day 30 counts in his tally.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה supports the rule from step 9 with a formal testimony from רבי פפייס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The testimony repeats the law, and it also adds the reason directly. Day 30 is counted as part of the tally for the second term. That one day is shared, so the second term can end on day 59.

keyTerms.meaning: A testimony, a formal report of a law received from earlier teachers
The תנא who gave this testimony
It counts for him as part of the tally

steps.whatToRemember: Day 30 of the first נזירות is shared: it finishes the first term and also starts the second.

phrases.english: And this testimony was given by Rabbi Pappeyas,
about one who vowed two terms of nezirus,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם גִּילַּח אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים —
phrases.english: that if he shaved for the first one on day thirty
he shaves for the second one on day sixty,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם גִּילַּח לְיוֹם שִׁשִּׁים חָסֵר אֶחָד — יָצָא,
phrases.english: and if he shaved on day sixty less one, he has fulfilled it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיּוֹם שֶׁל שְׁלֹשִׁים עוֹלֶה לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן.
phrases.english: because the thirtieth day counts for him in the tally.
phrases.notes: He means the tally of the second term.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the ruling in step 9 with a testimony and states its reason.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a second term can end on day 59 if the first term was ended on day 30
steps.raayaSupportSource: The testimony of רבי פפייס: the thirtieth day counts toward the tally

steps.title: A plain נזיר becomes טמא on day 30
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules on a plain נזיר who becomes טמא on day 30. The תנא קמא says he loses everything. רבי אליעזר says he loses only seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone said 'I am a נזיר' and became טמא on day 30, he loses the entire count. רבי אליעזר says he loses only seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks what happens when a plain נזיר becomes טמא on the very last day of his term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the טומאה on day 30 wipes out all 30 days, so he must start over. רבי אליעזר disagrees and says he loses only the seven days he needs to become טהור again. The משנה does not give reasons here; the גמרא will discuss them.

keyTerms.meaning: He became ritually impure, here from contact with a dead body
It cancels everything, so all the days he counted are lost
The תנא who disagrees with the first opinion
Seven, meaning the seven days of becoming טהור

steps.confusionAlert: 'Cancels only seven' does not mean seven days of his נזירות are erased. It means he only has to wait the seven days of becoming טהור.

phrases.english: One who said: 'I am hereby a nazir,'

phrases.aramaic: נִטְמָא יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים — סוֹתֵר אֶת הַכֹּל.
phrases.english: if he became impure on day thirty, it cancels everything.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ סוֹתֵר אֶלָּא שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: It cancels only seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁאָמַר הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר נִטְמָא יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: טומאה on day 30. It builds on the idea from step 8 that day 30 is a borderline day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says טומאה on day 30 cancels the whole term. רבי אליעזר says it cancels only seven days.

steps.title: טמא on the last day of a 30-day or 100-day term
steps.stepSummary: If he said 'thirty days' and became טמא on day 30, it cancels everything. If he said 'one hundred days' and became טמא on day 100, it cancels everything, but רבי אליעזר says it cancels only thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'I am a נזיר for thirty days' and became טמא on day 30, he loses everything. If he said 'I am a נזיר for one hundred days' and became טמא on day 100, he loses everything. רבי אליעזר says he loses only thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two more cases. In each one, the person stated a number of days and became טמא on the last day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the person says 'thirty days' outright, no one disagrees: טומאה on day 30 cancels everything. In the 100-day case, the תנא קמא again says everything is lost. רבי אליעזר says he loses only the last thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I am a נזיר for thirty days', a term that states its length
One hundred days

phrases.english: 'I am hereby a nazir for thirty days,'

phrases.aramaic: נִטְמָא יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים — סוֹתֵר אֶת הַכֹּל.
phrases.english: if he became impure on day thirty, it cancels everything.
'I am hereby a nazir for one hundred days,'

phrases.aramaic: נִטְמָא יוֹם מֵאָה — סוֹתֵר אֶת הַכֹּל.
phrases.english: if he became impure on day one hundred, it cancels everything.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ סוֹתֵר אֶלָּא שְׁלֹשִׁים.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: It cancels only thirty.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם נִטְמָא יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds cases where the person stated the length of his term.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a stated 30-day term, טומאה on day 30 cancels everything, and everyone agrees. In a 100-day term, טומאה on day 100 cancels everything according to the תנא קמא, but only thirty days according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: טמא on day 101, after the term but before shaving
steps.stepSummary: If he became טמא on day 101, it cancels thirty days. רבי אליעזר says only seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he became טמא on day 101, he loses thirty days. רבי אליעזר says he loses only seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its last case: the person became טמא just after his 100 days ended, before he shaved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here even the תנא קמא agrees that he does not lose everything, only thirty days. רבי אליעזר goes further and says he only needs the seven days of becoming טהור. In every case where רבי אליעזר argues, his view is one level easier than the תנא קמא's.

keyTerms.meaning: One hundred and one, the first day after the term ends

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is a ladder of cases. For the תנא קמא, טומאה on the last day of the term cancels everything, but טומאה after the term ends (day 101) cancels only thirty. Wherever רבי אליעזר argues, he is one level more lenient. In the stated 'thirty days' case he does not argue.

phrases.aramaic: נִטְמָא יוֹם מֵאָה וְאֶחָד — סוֹתֵר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: If he became impure on day one hundred and one, it cancels thirty days.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ סוֹתֵר אֶלָּא שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: It cancels only seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִטְמָא יוֹם מֵאָה וְאֶחָד סוֹתֵר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the טומאה one day later than in step 12, to just after the term ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טומאה on day 101 cancels thirty days according to the תנא קמא, and only seven according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the first case of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting the plain נזיר case: טמא on day 30 cancels everything, but רבי אליעזר says seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if someone said 'I am a נזיר' and became טמא on day 30, he loses everything. רבי אליעזר says he loses only seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by quoting the first line of the משנה. This is a setup line that prepares for the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is ruled here. The quote tells us which case the גמרא is about to examine: the argument about a plain נזיר who becomes טמא on day 30.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאָמַר ״הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר״ וְנִטְמָא יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים —
